{"world_model":"W1 (mechanism), after E011.

The setup
- The tip is E010. It is E008 (Muon on the conv filters with 3 Newton-Schulz steps, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, epochs=9.5, so 238 steps) with group 3 narrowed to 512 channels.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477. The margin over 0.753 is only 0.18 pp.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time. Accuracy is deterministic: E003 and E004 both gave 0.748633.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% more time (E005).
- LR floor 0.07 → 0: −0.08 pp (E009). It is redundant with the annealing done by the EMA.
- Muon: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time and −0.59 pp (E007).
- Epoch cut of 0.5: −0.18 pp and −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576 → 512: −4.8% time and −0.25 pp (E010).
- NEW, E011 (20/24/28/32 at 30/30/20/20%): −22% time but −0.97 pp. That is about twice the usual exchange rate.
  - Mechanism: at 20 px the group-3 maps are 2×2 after the 20→10→5→2 pooling, so features degrade much faster than the FLOPs shrink.
  - The shorter 32 px tail also leaves the final EMA anneal at mixed resolution, which adds a train/test resolution mismatch.
  - Conclusion: resolution has hit its floor. The exchange rate is about 0.45 pp per 10% for moderate cuts and worsens sharply past that.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: H2D copy, eigh, pad, and the per-epoch augment (a 25-way masked copy that syncs on the host) plus the interpolate.
- The variable part, about 6.2 s, is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step.
- CUDA graphs and graph-break removal can gain only 0-4%. Low-resolution steps have short kernels, so they gain the most. Max-autotune variants carry a risk of slowdowns (E003-style).
- My time misses are now mostly cases where the real cut was larger than I predicted (E009, E011). Real time tracks pixel share slightly better than linearly.

The accuracy model
- My scale for central points is now fine. My misses come from nonlinear regimes: extreme resolution (E011) and optimizer or averaging changes (E005, E006), where effects were larger than priors.
- Muon renormalizes the conv weights each step, so weight decay acts only on the BN biases and the head. Halving it should change little.
- Muon lr sets the angular step size. 0.24 was tuned for CIFAR-10 with a different step count, so ×1.5 could move accuracy either way by about 0.3 pp.
- LS 0.3 vs 0.2 with 100 classes: probably close to neutral, within ±0.3 pp.
- Plain EMA without the fast-weight reset loses the variance damping of Lookahead. The final window is short (decay about 0.77 per 5 steps), so it probably loses 0.1-0.4 pp.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe. Any kernel or RNG-path change reshuffles it by about ±0.2 pp.
- Time varies by about 1-2% between runs.
- Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548, the tip's 40-seed mean is roughly 85% likely to be at or above 0.75.

Unsure
- Whether seeds 0-2 sit high relative to held-out seeds (I016).
- Whether the per-epoch augment masked copy creates a measurable host stall under the 4-CPU pin.

W1 (mechanism), after E011.

The setup
- The tip is E010. It is E008 (Muon on the conv filters with 3 Newton-Schulz steps, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, epochs=9.5, so 238 steps) with group 3 narrowed to 512 channels.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477. The margin over 0.753 is only 0.18 pp.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time. Accuracy is deterministic: E003 and E004 both gave 0.748633.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% more time (E005).
- LR floor 0.07 → 0: −0.08 pp (E009). It is redundant with the annealing done by the EMA.
- Muon: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time and −0.59 pp (E007).
- Epoch cut of 0.5: −0.18 pp and −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576 → 512: −4.8% time and −0.25 pp (E010).
- NEW, E011 (20/24/28/32 at 30/30/20/20%): −22% time but −0.97 pp. That is about twice the usual exchange rate.
  - Mechanism: at 20 px the group-3 maps are 2×2 after the 20→10→5→2 pooling, so features degrade much faster than the FLOPs shrink.
  - The shorter 32 px tail also leaves the final EMA anneal at mixed resolution, which adds a train/test resolution mismatch.
  - Conclusion: resolution has hit its floor. The exchange rate is about 0.45 pp per 10% for moderate cuts and worsens sharply past that.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: H2D copy, eigh, pad, and the per-epoch augment (a 25-way masked copy that syncs on the host) plus the interpolate.
- The variable part, about 6.2 s, is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step.
- CUDA graphs and graph-break removal can gain only 0-4%. Low-resolution steps have short kernels, so they gain the most. Max-autotune variants carry a risk of slowdowns (E003-style).
- My time misses are now mostly cases where the real cut was larger than I predicted (E009, E011). Real time tracks pixel share slightly better than linearly.

The accuracy model
- My scale for central points is now fine. My misses come from nonlinear regimes: extreme resolution (E011) and optimizer or averaging changes (E005, E006), where effects were larger than priors.
- Muon renormalizes the conv weights each step, so weight decay acts only on the BN biases and the head. Halving it should change little.
- Muon lr sets the angular step size. 0.24 was tuned for CIFAR-10 with a different step count, so ×1.5 could move accuracy either way by about 0.3 pp.
- LS 0.3 vs 0.2 with 100 classes: probably close to neutral, within ±0.3 pp.
- Plain EMA without the fast-weight reset loses the variance damping of Lookahead. The final window is short (decay about 0.77 per 5 steps), so it probably loses 0.1-0.4 pp.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe. Any kernel or RNG-path change reshuffles it by about ±0.2 pp.
- Time varies by about 1-2% between runs.
- Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548, the tip's 40-seed mean is roughly 85% likely to be at or above 0.75.

Unsure
- Whether seeds 0-2 sit high relative to held-out seeds (I016).
- Whether the per-epoch augment masked copy creates a measurable host stall under the 4-CPU pin.
- Whether a Muon lr or LS retune hides a gain of 0.3 pp or more that could buy back about 0.5 epoch.

forecasts.reason: The run is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step, so only launch gaps are removed (about 2-3%). The Lookahead foreach ops and the Python-side LR writes make it hard to capture the full step cleanly.
No recipe change. Expect the held-out seeds within about 0.2 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean, with seed std about 0.25 pp.
LS mostly reshapes the logit margin. With 100 classes and an EMA endpoint, 0.3 vs 0.2 should differ by less than 0.3 pp.
The weights are fixed-norm, so lr sets the angular step size. ×1.5 at 238 steps may help or hurt; ±0.3 pp is plausible.
Muon renormalizes the conv weights, so weight decay only affects the BN biases and the head. Expect a small effect, mostly reshuffle noise.
The code already uses steps=3, so as described this is a no-op. Even going to 2 steps would save under 2%.
The masked-copy augment and the LR writes cost a little per epoch, but the GPU is saturated. Expect a cut of 1-3%, below the 3% bar.
Dropping the reset loses Lookahead's variance damping. The short final EMA window gives about −0.2 pp, which sits right at the 0.3 pp tolerance.

cruxes: Do held-out seeds 3-12 (I016) put the tip's mean below 0.7545? If so, the next step must rebuild margin before cutting time.
Does any time-neutral optimizer lever (Muon lr, LS) give +0.3 pp or more, which could be spent as about 0.75 epoch (about 7% time)?
What share of the per-step time is GPU idle under the 4-CPU pin (I021 profile)? It decides whether CUDA graphs or fusion work can beat 3%.
